chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Hasan ibn Musa, from Muhammad ibn al-Subbakh, from some of our companions, who said:

Al-Rabi' came to Abu Ja'far al-Mansur while he was caliphal and performing tawaf. He said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, so-and-so, your mawla, died yesterday, and so-and-so cut off his head after his death.' He said: 'He became furious and angry.'
He said to Ibn Shubrumah, Ibn Abi Layla, and a number of judges and jurists: 'What do you say about this?' Each one said: 'We have nothing regarding this.'

He said: 'So he kept repeating the question, saying: 'Should I kill him or not?' They said: 'We have nothing regarding this, but a man has just arrived. If anyone has an answer, it is with him, and he is Ja'far ibn Muhammad, and he has entered al-Mas'a.'
He said to al-Rabi': 'Go to him and tell him: 'If we did not know of your preoccupation with what you are in, we would have asked you to come to us, but answer us regarding such and such.'

Al-Rabi' came to him while he was on al-Marwah and conveyed the message to him. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'You see the preoccupation I am in, and the jurists and scholars are with you, so ask them.'
He said to him: 'I have asked them, and they had nothing regarding it.'
He sent him back to him and said: 'I ask you for what you did not answer us with, for the people have nothing regarding this.'
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Until I finish what I am in.'
When he finished, he sat on the side of al-Masjid al-Haram and said to al-Rabi': 'Go and tell him: 'Upon him is one hundred dinars.'
He said: 'And he conveyed that to him, and they said to him: 'Ask him how it became upon him one hundred dinars.'

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'In the nutfah (drop), twenty dinars; in the 'alaqah (clot), twenty; in the mudghah (chewed lump), twenty dinars; in the 'adam (bones), twenty dinars; and in the lahm (flesh), twenty dinars.'
Then We developed him into another creation, and this is he who is dead, in the same status as before the soul was blown into him in his mother's womb as a fetus.'
He said: 'So he returned to them and informed them of the answer, and they were pleased with that.'
He said: 'And they said: 'Return to him and ask him: 'To whom are the dinars? Are they for his heirs or not?'

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'His heirs have nothing in it. This is something that came to him in his hand after his death; it is used to perform hajj on his behalf or is spent in a path of goodness.'

He said: 'The man claimed that they sent back the messenger, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) answered him regarding it with thirty-six questions, and the man remembered only the extent of this answer.'
ai.seo_question: What is the blood money for a person whose head is cut off after death according to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from *al-Istibsar* highlights the jurisprudential independence of the Imams, as Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) provided a unique ruling on post-mortem amputation when the Abbasid jurists were stumped. By linking the blood money to the five stages of fetal development, the Imam grounded the compensation in the biological reality of the body's formation, distinguishing it from the soul's infusion. The ruling that the *diyah* is for the deceased's own benefit (e.g., Hajj or charity) rather than inheritance underscores the Shia view of the body's sanctity and the specific nature of this compensation.
